prompt.brief: Design a real-time fraud decisioning platform that combines rules, ML, graph and behavioral signals, adapts to new patterns, and returns explainable allow/review/deny decisions without blocking legitimate transactions.
successSignals: Define the transaction decision contract, feature freshness, entity graph, rules/model versions, action thresholds, reason codes, and review lifecycle.
Keep the synchronous path bounded with precomputed behavior features; handle duplicate requests, unknown outcomes, delayed labels, and provider timeouts.
Separate scoring from case management, training, feedback, regulatory reporting, and model rollout; make decisions reproducible and auditable.
Explain latency/recall tradeoffs, bias, privacy, adversarial adaptation, failover, observability, and safe pending/manual-review behavior.

functional: Score payment or account events, combine rules and model signals, return allow/review/deny with reason codes, and persist the decision evidence.
Maintain entity relationships and velocity features, open investigator cases, accept labels/chargebacks, and generate compliance reports.
Support idempotent retries, model/rule rollback, privacy controls, feedback loops, delayed labels, and provider or feature-store failure.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 scoring latency under 50ms with a documented failover decision and preserve evidence for every outcome.
Scale to 100k transactions per second and high-cardinality entity graphs without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Real-time fraud decisioning platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Real-time fraud decisioning platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Real-time fraud decisioning platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Real-time fraud decisioning platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Real-time fraud decisioning platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Real-time fraud decisioning platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Real-time fraud decisioning platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Real-time fraud decisioning platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Real-time fraud decisioning platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
